A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LION and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and CIFAR-100 experiments, C4/GLUE evaluations, LRA ablations, and OpenWebText language-modeling results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds chunk-size sensitivity, a ViT-Chunk memory comparison, and learned decay-factor analyses.

M1.justification: The central full-attention, bidirectional-RNN, and chunkwise procedures remain. The stated query/key feature map changes from normalized SiLU(x+0.5) in v1 Section 3.3 to normalized (SiLU(x)+0.5) in v2 Section 3.2. This changes the specified nonlinearity, although the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The datasets and principal tasks remain unchanged. However, v2 removes the explicit ImageNet accuracy evaluation below and above the 224-pixel training resolution from v1 Section D.11 and Figure 13. Resolution-dependent resource benchmarks remain; newly mentioned biological applications are not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds ViT-Chunk to the inference-memory comparison. The separate CIFAR-100 comparison involving unidirectional GRFA and RetNet and their bidirectional mappings in v1 Table 17 is removed. The principal vision, MLM, and LRA comparator sets remain; additional theoretical mappings are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled chunk-size sweep at image resolution 1248. It also revises Hydra's reported base-scale parameter count from 104M in v1 Table 1 to 91M in v2 Table 2, without establishing a rerun. The main training budgets, MLM preprocessing, and GLUE recipes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds chunk-size sensitivity analysis in Figure 4 and learned decay-factor analysis in Figure 12. It removes the resolution-transfer accuracy study and the separate GRFA/RetNet mapping ablation. The extensive LRA, positional-embedding, finetuning-recipe, distillation, and directional ablations are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: The OpenWebText perplexities retain the same reported plus/minus uncertainties in v1 Figure 4 and v2 Figure 5. No new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced. The new decay-factor plots describe learned parameters rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: The principal ImageNet, C4/GLUE, LRA, and OpenWebText performance numbers are retained. New results include the ViT-Chunk memory curve, chunk-size memory/latency trends, and decay-factor distributions. Conversely, v1 Table 17's GRFA/RetNet comparison results and Figure 13's resolution-accuracy curves are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix B.5 adds substantial diagonal-decay derivations and Theorems B.1–B.2 beyond v1's brief tensor-mask extension in C.7. Appendix B.7 introduces an explicit DeltaNet treatment, and additional model mappings expand the formal scope. v2 also corrects the causal softmax mask from multiplicative to additive; most existing scalar and chunkwise derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens the performance claim from approaching Transformer/SSM performance to matching or exceeding softmax Transformers. v2 also emphasizes LION as a unified framework for a broad model class. The central equivalence, efficient inference, and chunkwise trade-off contributions were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds the qualification that DeltaNet's cubic-cost matrix inverse undermines fast full-attention training, and clarifies architectural differences from Hydra. Its limitations discussion replaces v1's kernel-optimization and unstable-activation concerns with possible gating and model-scaling extensions. The removed resolution-transfer study also loses its associated interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's image-memory measurement batch size of 64 and MLM timing procedure using batch size 32 over 60 batches. It adds a practical chunk-count guideline and explicitly describes substituting LION into DeiT/BERT without other configuration changes. Most hardware, training hyperparameters, recipe information, and code access remain.

R1.justification: The detailed related-work appendix and several associated discussions and citations are removed. v2 adds positioning around biological applications, vision scanning, diagonal recurrence complexity, and additional model families. It explicitly positions LION-S as a Gated RFA extension differing in its nonlinearity, revising v1's predominantly Mamba-2-inspired description.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Mask construction is integrated into the full-attention presentation, the appendices are reorganized with a table of contents, the dedicated related-work section disappears, and limitations move to the appendix. These changes substantially alter the document's organization and explanation.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one column. ImageNet and GLUE tables are restructured or merged, an accuracy-versus-speed scatter plot is added, and architecture and inference-trade-off figures move into the main text. The chunking illustration is redrawn, alongside genuinely added and removed analysis plots.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation and adds useful chunk-size and decay diagnostics, but removes validation studies and timing details. Stronger performance statements are not consistently supported: Section 4.2 claims all LION models outperform ViT, while Table 2 retains base LION-LIT at 74.7 versus ViT at 77.9. The new Theorem B.2 also describes an unscaled recurrence while retaining a scaling denominator in Eq. 84. These substantive benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
